newsitem.title: UK: North Sea oil platform drifts, no danger reported.
newsitem.headline: North Sea oil platform drifts, no danger reported.

text.p: A North Sea oil rig platform with 69 people on board began to drift on Tuesday about 80 miles (130 km) east of the Scottish coast but the situation was not regarded as hazardous, coastguards said.
The rig, the Sedco Explorer, began drifting after a tow line parted in high seas and fierce gales.
Efforts were under way to reconnect the tow line to a tug, said the coastguards in the Scottish city of Aberdeen.
A British Air Force helicopter and a reconnaissance aircraft have been placed on standby.
No other details were immediately available.
Gales and heavy rain lashed Britain overnight, injuring several people, blocking roads and leaving thousands of homes without power, emergency services said.
No independent confirmation was available of a report by Britain's Press Association news agency that four people had been killed as the gales wreaked havoc with gusts of up to 145 kph (90 mph).
